title: Return None for missing users instead of raising
body:
Fixes #88. `fetch_user` raised `HTTPError` on 404, which crashed the admin page when a user was soft-deleted. Now 404 maps to `None`; other errors still raise. Added a timeout while here (same value as the rest of the client).

Tested with `pytest tests/test_api.py` (new test for the 404 case).

files.patch:
@@ -10,7 +10,12 @@ def fetch_user(user_id):
-    return api.get(f"/users/{user_id}")
+    resp = api.get(f"/users/{user_id}", timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT)
+    if resp.status_code == 404:
+        # The upstream returns 404 for soft-deleted users too; treat both as "not found".
+        return None
+    resp.raise_for_status()
+    return resp.json()

@@ -30,0 +31,8 @@
+def test_fetch_user_404_returns_none(mock_api):
+    mock_api.get.return_value.status_code = 404
+    assert fetch_user(7) is None
+
+
+def test_fetch_user_500_raises(mock_api):
+    mock_api.get.return_value.raise_for_status.side_effect = HTTPError
+    with pytest.raises(HTTPError):
+        fetch_user(7)

commit_messages:
Return None for 404 in fetch_user

Soft-deleted users return 404 upstream; the admin page crashed on them.
Add tests for fetch_user error paths
